summary_paragraph: Mr. ___ was admitted for feeling unwell, with abdominal discomfort, poor appetite, and generalized weakness. Evaluation showed no acute infection, as urine culture revealed no growth, and labs were stable. His symptoms were attributed to a combination of chronic conditions, including malignant neoplasm of the kidney, bladder atony, benign prostatic hypertrophy, diabetes, coronary atherosclerosis, and depressive disorder. He was managed supportively with nutritional supplementation, initiation of an antidepressant, and optimization of chronic disease medications. There was no need for surgical or procedural intervention. He was discharged home with home health services, follow-up appointments, and instructions for catheter care, medication adherence, and symptom monitoring.
problems: Malignant neoplasm of kidney, except pelvis
Coronary atherosclerosis of unspecified type of vessel, native or graft
Diabetes mellitus without mention of complication, type II or unspecified type, not stated as uncontrolled
Hypertrophy (benign) of prostate without urinary obstruction and other lower urinary tract symptom (LUTS)
